newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks shrug Dow to inch up at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks shrug Dow to inch up at close.

text.p: Mexican stocks rose for the first time in three sessions Friday despite a big drop on Wall Street.
The leading IPC share index ended up 3.16 points at 3,890.36. Trading volume was lackluster at 73.6 million shares.

"Volume was not bad, but you could see caution in there. Next week's data will be crucial for deciding whether to step into the market or not," Hector Jimenez, analyst at the Inverlat brokerage, said.

Mexico's Finance Ministry is expected to announce first quarter GDP on Monday, May 19. Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz told journalists Thursday he expected GDP to grow by 4.5 percent to 5.0 percent. This compares with growth of 5.12 percent forecast on average in a Reuters survey.
Traders said selective buying helped bolster the market and resist the slide on the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which dropped 138.88 points to 7,194.67.
"When the Dow began to slide, we followed suit, but pushing and shoving at the close was due to selective buying that propped it up," one trader said.
Financial stock Bancomer contributed most to propping up the market, gaining three centavos (less than 1 cent) to 2.94 pesos (37 cents).
Telmex ended off two centavos (less than 1 cent) at 17.12 pesos ($2.17), while its ADRs declined 1/4 to 43-3/8.
Traders also drew attention to retail stock Soriana, up 1.20 pesos (15 cents) to 19.00 pesos ($2.41) in brisk trade.
Dealers said interest in the stock, which made an infrequent appearance on the most-traded stocks list, was enhanced by a long-term buy recommendation issued by the Serfin financial group.
In the broad market, 106 stocks changed hands, of which gainers outnumbered loser by 50 to 38.

Analysts said the market could begin to rally once uncertainy over U.S. interest rates had receded. The Federal Reserve, the U.S., central bank, meets on Tuesday to weigh its next move on interest rates.
"I don't rule out new records at the end of next week," Jimenez said.
